mappings.note: Both contain the superscription: 'To the choirmaster', 'Lilies' (Shoshannim), 'Sons of Korah', 'Maskil/Lesson song', 'Love song/Wedding song'. The Norwegian uses 'En læresang. En kjærlighetssang' while French uses 'Maskil... cantique nuptial', but the content is equivalent.
Content matches: Heart overflowing/excellent word, work for the king, tongue like a skilled scribe's pen.
Content matches: Most beautiful of men, grace on lips, God blessed forever.
Content matches: Gird sword at hip, mighty warrior, splendor and glory.

The translation adds 'monte sur ton char' (mount your chariot) which is not explicitly in the Norwegian text ('Ri frem seierrik...'). However, the core message of riding forth for truth/humility/righteousness and the right hand showing terrible deeds matches. The addition is minor contextually.
Content matches: Sharp arrows pierce king's enemies' hearts, peoples fall under you. (Order of clauses differs slightly but content is identical).
Content matches: Throne stands forever, scepter of righteousness.
Content matches: Love justice/hate wickedness, God anointed with oil of joy above fellows (feller/semblables).
Content matches: Clothes smell of myrrh/aloe/cassia, ivory palaces, string music.
Content matches: Kings' daughters among precious ones, queen at right side with Ophir gold. (French specifies 'épouse' for the queen, Norwegian says 'Dronningen', meaning is consistent).
Content matches: Listen daughter, incline ear, forget people and father's house.
Content matches: King desires beauty, he is lord, bow to him.
Content matches: Daughter of Tyre with gifts, rich seek favor. (French adds 'viendront te rendre hommage' which is implied by 'søker din gunst').
Content matches: King's daughter full of glory inside, dress woven with gold embroidery.
Content matches: Brought to king in embroidered clothes, virgins companions brought to you.
Content matches: Brought with joy and gladness, enter king's palace.
Content matches: Sons take place of fathers, appointed princes over the earth.
This verse exists in the French translation but has no corresponding text in the provided OSMAIN (Norwegian) text. The Norwegian text ends at verse 17.

extraContent.description: Je rendrai ton nom célèbre dans tous les âges; aussi les peuples t'honoreront à toujours, à perpétuité. (I will make your name famous in all ages; so the peoples will honor you forever and ever.)
